Build SFS for all samples in a WithinHostExperiment

Source: R/sfs.R
buildSFSList.Rd

Convenience wrapper that calls buildSFS for each sample and returns a named list of WithinHostSFS objects.

Usage

buildSFSList(
  whe,
  nBins = 20L,
  fold = TRUE,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE,
  threshold = 0.03,
  genomeLength = NULL
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment.

nBins

Integer. Number of frequency bins, a whole number of at least 1 (default: 20).

fold

Logical. If TRUE, fold the SFS to minor allele frequency (0 to 0.5), giving polarization = "none". If FALSE, bin the alternative allele frequency from 0 to 1, treating the reference allele as ancestral (polarization = "reference"). Default: TRUE.

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE, only use QC-passed variants. Default: TRUE. The spectrum's maxFreq slot then records the smallest maxFreq among the filters applied with flagISNV, above which no call can appear; with the default ISNVFilter that is 0.5, so an unfolded spectrum is empty above 0.5. To keep the high-frequency classes, flag the unfiltered object with maxFreq = 1: flagISNV() adds to the flags already set, so it cannot restore calls that an earlier filter with a lower maxFreq removed.

threshold

Numeric. Detection threshold (default: 0.03). The first bin starts at this value, not 0. It must be at least 0 and below the top of the spectrum: 0.5 when folded, 1 otherwise.

genomeLength

Integer (optional). The genome length that the per-site statistics of neutralityFromSFS divide by. By default it is read from seqlengths(rowRanges(whe)), summed over every recorded sequence as in calcDiversity, and is NA when that is not recorded. The spectrum itself does not depend on it.

Value

A named list of WithinHostSFS objects.

Examples

data(example_whe)
sfs_list <- buildSFSList(example_whe, genomeLength = 1000L)
length(sfs_list)
#> [1] 3
